A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TADA and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The material matches reliably after accounting for pagination and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet experiments with EDM/EDM2, SD3 text-to-image evaluations, ablations and generated examples, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative experiments, ablations and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the augmented dynamics, pretrained-model input transformation, force term and sampling procedure are unchanged. Added explanations do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-64 and ImageNet-512 generation and SD3 text-to-image generation using HPSv2 benchmark prompts. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 5–6 retain DPM-Solver++, UniPC and the Heun reference lines. Figure 7 retains UniPC-ODE and SA-SDE; DPM-Solver++ remains excluded from the SD3 comparison.

E3.justification: Solver orders, SNR discretization, baseline configuration searches, noise limits, CFG settings and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendix C in v1 matches Appendix D in v2.

E4.justification: The prior-scale diversity analysis in Figure 3, augmented-dimension comparison in Figure 5, and qualitative comparisons in Figures 4 and 8–10 are retained. No additional ablation, robustness test or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report SD3 means and standard deviations over three random seeds, with 3,200 images per seed. Figure 7 retains the same uncertainty bands; no statistical procedure or reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The quantitative plots, embedded numerical labels and generated examples are identical, including appendix Figures 9–10. The reported rankings, dimension-dependent findings and CFG trends also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The propositions, equations and appendix proofs are retained without substantive mathematical changes. The expanded Kronecker-product notation guidance and explanation of the existing pseudo-noise term clarify presentation rather than revise the theory.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit assertion that simple noise or noisy-data augmentation with diffusion loss offers no training benefit, including beyond momentum diffusion. v1 stated training equivalence and discussed augmentation advantages less explicitly. The abstract, sampling contributions and speed claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The introduction now qualifies the SDE-over-ODE fidelity advantage as occurring with sufficient function evaluations and limiting model capacity. This narrows the earlier introductory statement and aligns it with the capacity-related discussion already present. The detailed conclusions and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The code-access link, baseline implementation sources, noise limits, configuration-search grids and HPSv2.1 evaluation detail are unchanged. The expanded notation guidance adds no implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The same 36 references are retained. The introduction modestly broadens positioning by explicitly presenting training equivalence as a negative conclusion about simple augmentation approaches beyond momentum diffusion, while emphasizing sampling as the source of benefit.

P1.justification: v2 expands the contribution bullets, explains pseudo-noise near Proposition 3.3, and promotes the existing appendix notation paragraph into an expanded Appendix A. Subsequent appendices are renumbered, and the publication footer changes. Most prose and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1’s caption adds data-prediction and multiple-variable clarification. Text and equations reflow, and Table 1 moves relative to surrounding prose. All ten figure graphics and both tables’ substantive contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through the main-text pseudo-noise explanation, expanded notation guidance and qualified SDE comparison. The method, proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged. The broader no-training-benefit wording adds no validation, so the improvement is limited to exposition and framing.
